children: New Delhi, Nov. 13 -- Drone manufacturer ideaForge Technology has delivered a sharp turnaround in its quarterly performance, returning to profitability in the September quarter as revenue more than doubled year-on-year.

However, the stock's recovery has not been entirely smooth, with shares witnessing intermittent selling pressure despite gaining over 50% in the past year. With the company showing signs of financial improvement and technical indicators offering mixed signals, investors are now assessing whether the stock has further room to climb or whether caution is warranted at current levels.
ideaForge shares have declined 6% over the past month, 9% in three months and 8% in six months. Over the past year, the stock has gained 53%.
The shares touched a 52-week high of Rs.997 in June 2026 and a 52-week low of Rs.367.95 in March 2026, highlighting the volatility witnessed during the period.

ideaForge Technology reported a net profit of Rs.6.5 crore for the September quarter, compared with a net loss of Rs.19.6 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Revenue from operations increased 124% year-on-year to Rs.91 crore in Q2 FY27, from Rs.40.8 crore a year earlier.

The company's earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) stood at Rs.23 crore, compared with a loss at the operating level in the year-ago quarter. The return to profitability, alongside strong revenue growth, marked a significant improvement in its quarterly performance.

Despite the improvement in quarterly earnings, investors need to assess whether the stock's technical structure supports further gains. Analysts have identified key resistance levels that could determine its next move, while their recommendations range from avoiding fresh purchases to accumulating the stock for a potential move towards higher targets.

Jigar S Patel, Senior Manager - Technical Research at Anand Rathi Share and Stock Brokers, has advised investors to avoid fresh buying at current levels. He identified support at Rs.675 and resistance at Rs.728, where the 200-day exponential moving average (DEMA) and monthly resistance coincide.
"The technical structure remains cautious as the stock has been unable to sustain its RSI above the 60 mark, indicating a lack of strong bullish momentum," Patel said.

The stock's RSI was around 51, indicating neutral momentum. Patel believes the upside could remain restricted unless shares decisively cross the 200 DEMA and sustain above Rs.728. Until then, he recommended a wait-and-watch approach.

Deepesh Sarawagi, Technical Research Analyst at Choice Broking, offered a more constructive assessment, identifying early signs of a structural bottoming formation. He pointed to positive RSI divergence as the stock formed lower lows near the Rs.620-630 support zone while the RSI made higher lows, suggesting fading selling pressure.
" A decisive daily close above the Rs.730- Rs.735 barrier will confirm a bullish reversal, potentially triggering an upside move toward the Rs.780- Rs.800 resistance zone," Sarawagi said.

He noted that the stock had reclaimed its 200-day and 20-day EMAs but was consolidating below the 50-day and 100-day EMAs around Rs.717-730. Immediate support was placed at Rs.660-630, followed by major structural support near Rs.630.

Meanwhile, Bharat K Gala, Head of Technical at Ventura, has recommended a Buy on ideaForge, with a target price of Rs.900 against the last close of Rs.714.15. He placed support levels at Rs.692-676, Rs.665 and Rs.653-635, with a stop loss of Rs.617.
"RSI trading above 50, MACD shows positive momentum & PVT indicates the positive uptrend - signs of buying," Gala said.

According to Ventura, the stock had broken out of a descending channel on the daily chart, supported by volumes and a bullish candle that reached Rs.733.45 in November 2026. The brokerage also highlighted the formation of higher bottoms and a move above the 200-day simple moving average as signs of improving momentum.
